lines.text: Today you can walk into a public library and borrow thousands of dollars in books completely free.
For centuries, books were rare luxury items owned exclusively by wealthy aristocrats and churches.
In seventeen thirty-one, Benjamin Franklin and his friends pooled their money to launch America's first subscription lending library.
Members paid annual dues to share a communal collection of history, science, and philosophy books.
In the nineteenth century, cities introduced tax-supported free libraries open to all citizens regardless of wealth.
Steel magnate Andrew Carnegie personally funded over twenty-five hundred free public libraries across the globe.
Public libraries remain one of the purest sanctuaries of free knowledge in human history.
